report:
PASS for the entire stated big rational surface theorem and the additional range with numerically zero canonical positive part. This does not establish unrestricted P16.5. I independently checked S1–S8 and Appendices A–E; historical verdicts, source hashes, compilation and visual checks supply no mathematical premise. G0 is used only in its task-granted actual ample domain. The unindexed urn passage records that grant; every numbered passage indexes the external premises below.

The surface decomposition proof is sound. Coordinatewise maxima preserve the finite polytope of nef subdivisors; maximality gives orthogonality, and the nonnegative maximal-eigenvector argument proves negative definiteness. The inverse-sign calculation establishes numerical minimality and actual section division, including ceiling multiplicities and entire section systems. The negative supports of decreasing ample perturbations are nested and each has at most dim N¹ curves, so their union is finite. Bounded coefficients, nef closedness and the rational linear system give the canonical rational limit without assuming a section of the original pseudoeffective bundle. The volume proof handles every permissible degree through finitely many residual twists, rather than relying only on a divisible subsequence. Riemann–Roch and duality establish vol(L)=P², positive when L is big.

The arbitrary-field scope of the algebraic inputs is valid. In particular, finite dimensionality can be checked by descending any finite independent collection of divisors and detecting curves to a finitely generated characteristic-zero field and embedding that finite data into C. Their intersection-matrix rank is bounded by the fixed model's finite second Betti number. This adds no cardinality restriction.

The genuine-cone argument avoids the rejected flattening lemma. Finite continuous ample regularizers with positive tolerances form one directed decreasing net by compact open-cover comparison with finite continuous old minima. This proves the nef intersection description and compactness independently. Actual division after tensoring into fixed L+εH, varying-nef compactness and common-ample determination then establish PSH(L)=σ_N+PSH(P) at every analytic point. Both sides are already genuine before determination is invoked. Translation gives compactness, arbitrary decreasing closure, the reference σ_N and actual relative floors. Its injectivity reconstructs compensator values even at shared poles; no subtraction of infinities defines those values.

The intrinsic operator construction retains its required domain. Bounded nef inputs lie in a verified ample finite-energy space, so signed pairing and measure constructions apply. Positive ample perturbations establish positivity and raw intersection mass; exact measure-polynomial coefficient extraction gives Borel winning-set locality. Model coefficients retain ord_F(t). For normalized intrinsic u, strict-winning floor restrictions increase, and the estimate ||M_P(u_j)−M_P(u)||TV≤6(−E_P(u))/j gives full mass V and auxiliary independence. Positive mixed-height expansion proves integrability of every intrinsic finite-energy test. Uniform weight tails are established before numerical inequalities are extended through intrinsic floors. Subset-average polarization, mixed coefficient locality and complementary-mass bounds identify the actual mixed floor limits. Uniform floor errors then prove arbitrary directed-net convergence against the full original continuous test space.

The merely integrable decreasing-weight assertion also checks out. Define the extended mixed height by infimizing simultaneous bounded floors. For a fixed bounded weight floor, the established weighted limits identify its integral with H(weight,entries)−H(0,entries). Commuting the floor infima and using ordinary countable monotone convergence extends this identity to an arbitrary genuine weight, including an infinite integral. The reference height is finite for intrinsic finite-energy entries. Fixed-floor continuity and monotonicity prove decreasing continuity of these extended heights. Endpoint integrability therefore yields finite stage integrals and convergence of total weighted integrals. Only after this antecedent is established does the lsc weighted-measure lemma give weighted weak convergence. No unbounded intrinsic potential is placed in auxiliary ample E¹.

The envelope and derivative arguments are valid. Compact maxima and closed divisorial constraints construct genuine envelopes; PL difference representations promote continuous-obstacle order to all points. Ample supporting inequalities pass through bounded nef limits and then decreasing continuous majorants. Perturbed intrinsic envelopes have uniformly close bounded floors and uniform mass errors. This proves both outer derivatives at every intrinsic base for every original C⁰ direction. The uniform bounded-height coefficient estimate establishes weak energy upper semicontinuity and compact cost sublevels. The quadratic contraction estimate, decreasing convex-series argument and scaling prove precisely the claimed dual-finiteness/integrability equivalence and coercivity.

The polar argument retains the essential t² factor in the surface capacity criterion. The convex transform with exponent α<1/3 has finite intrinsic energy and exactly the original poles. Separately, S3 constructs the required actual negative-divisor pole test: Riemann–Roch gives an actual P=δH+D, and a section of qδH−ceil(N), multiplied by the canonical divisor sections, produces a P-section vanishing on all of Supp N. Its genuine bounded floors and quadratic contraction force D_P(ν)=∞ whenever ν assigns positive mass to the analytic pole set. Consequently targets and preconstructed top/mixed outputs exclude that set before any relative equation is solved.

The attainment proof's additional antecedents are established. The ample-plus-divisor decomposition is actual, and the bounded approximants are continuous rational PL genuine nef potentials without asserting fixed-P generation or semiampleness. The common ample class Ω=2θ+c₁(A) contains the relevant bounded inputs. Increasing-floor continuity and strong addition/mixed-pairing continuity are used within this ample domain; signed expansion then recovers θ-energy and I convergence. Target integrals converge using continuous-majorant Radon approximation and scalar divisor collars. The PL-direction estimate gives a uniform quadratic outer error, so maximizing measures approach the target on every original continuous test. The resulting target-comparison bound is uniform on costs. Since bounded PL model outputs have finite divisorial support with the actual component coefficients, their integral functionals are continuous in the stated topology. Uniform approximation proves target-integral continuity on compact cost sublevels and hence actual variational attainment.

Finite divisorial atomic attainment is independently proved before general-target continuity is used. Its solutions, the four-point estimate and common-ample determination establish all-point I separation. Thus equality of the original operators gives uniqueness modulo constants. Removing the actual fixed horizontal N factor identifies the local moving intersections with the preconstructed P products; zero polar mass specifies their extension, and relative floors construct the entire unbounded relative operator. The exact identities for energy, compensator, envelope and dual then transport attainment and both derivatives. Comparison uses fixed-Borel polynomial coefficients followed by total-variation floors. Domination uses zero ordered energy difference, I separation and the translation coefficient V>0 to remove the final constant.

For the additional zero-volume range, integer scaling and compact divisorial bounds force every numerically zero nef potential to be constant. Hence the whole relative cone is σ_N+R, its actual moving product and energy are zero, and the sole positive target is zero; uniqueness follows from rigidity. The bounded nonconstant O(1,0) example on P¹×P¹ has zero model top product and energy, correctly obstructing broader zero-mass uniqueness. No probability normalization at zero volume is used.

Harmless corrections are required in the cited printed formulas: the reversed height difference in BJ 7.21(ii), the locality cross-reference to 7.21(ii), the missing j=0 telescoping term in 7.30, and the stated pairing-degree/index corrections in 3.31, 3.33 and 7.38. Polarization uses its usual factorial coefficient; its omission in a displayed source estimate affects only the dimensional constant. BE 8.6's displayed curvature difference requires a minus sign, with its absolute-value bound unchanged. In S7 the floor winning sets increase exactly to {v<w}; the qualification about common poles is unnecessary. These are typographical corrections, not substantial repairs to the submitted argument.

On a projective surface over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for actual ample ω and a,b,c,d∈E¹(ω), BJ’s volume-normalized e,μ,I,J,J_b satisfy I(a,b)/3≤J_b(a)≤2I(a,b)/3, I(a,c)≲I(a,b)+I(b,c), |∫(a−b)d(μ_c−μ_d)|≲I(a,b)^(1/4)I(c,d)^(1/2)B^(1/4), |J_c(a)−J_c(b)|≲I(a,b)^(1/4)max(J(a),J(b),J(c))^(3/4), and e((a+b)/2)−(e(a)+e(b))/2≳I(a,b), where B=max{J(a),J(b),J(c),J(d)} and constants depend only on dimension. BJ v4, 7.27–7.31.

On a projective surface over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, rational PL functions are C⁰-dense, have test-configuration representatives, and lie in span_Q FS(A) for every actual ample rational A. Within actual ample E¹ classes, normalized strong convergence is equivalent to weak-plus-energy convergence and to I→0; addition and mixed heights are strongly continuous; increasing nets with a divisorial E¹ endpoint have mixed-height convergence. BJ v4, 2.2, 2.7, 2.26, 7.34–7.38 and 12.4.

On a compact Hausdorff space K, if positive Radon measures μ_i→μ weakly, lsc functions f_i increase to f, f_i∈L¹(μ_i), f∈L¹(μ), and ∫f_i dμ_i→∫f dμ, then f_i μ_i→f μ weakly. BJ v4, Lemma 7.22.

For a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, possibly trivially valued, continuous psh-regularizable metrics have symmetric multiadditive positive curvature products of intersection mass, continuous under uniform convergence and compatible with complete-field pushforward. Differences give signed continuous dpsh products and Deligne pairings; model Deligne metrics agree with the algebraic model pairing. Continuous psh metrics on semiample rational bundles are psh-regularizable. Boucksom–Eriksson v3, 7.14, 8.3–8.8, 8.16 and 8.18.
